name: Founders Fund

summary.text: Founders Fund is a San Francisco venture capital firm founded in 2005 and run by PayPal co-founders including Peter Thiel, Luke Nosek and Ken Howery. Its portfolio includes SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Stripe and Facebook. In 2008 its $20 million investment was SpaceX's first outside funding.

facts.claim: Anduril Industries was founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Trae Stephens (a Founders Fund partner), Matt Grimm and Joe Chen, and Founders Fund is an investor. The company is known for autonomous surveillance towers deployed at the U.S. southern border and builds autonomous military systems.

facts.claim: In August 2008, just after SpaceX's third consecutive Falcon 1 launch failure, Founders Fund invested $20 million in SpaceX, and Founders Fund partner Luke Nosek joined SpaceX's board.

sources.title: PayPal Co-Founders Invest $20 Million in SpaceX

facts.claim: In April 2025 CNBC reported, citing an SEC filing, that Founders Fund had closed Founders Fund Growth III, a $4.6 billion late-stage venture fund with capital from 270 investors, up from a $3.4 billion growth fund closed in early 2022. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that a substantial amount of the capital came from the firm's general partners. Cooley LLP, which advised on the fund, announced the close in August 2025.
facts.quote: The fund, Founders Fund Growth III, includes capital from 270 investors, the filing said.

facts.claim: Founders Fund joined Carbyne's $15 million Series B round in August 2018, which Calcalist described as the firm's first investment in Israel; Carbyne's backers at the time included former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak. In January 2021 Carbyne raised a $25 million Series B1 led by Hanaco Ventures and Elsted Capital Partners, with participation from former CIA Director David Petraeus and all existing investors including Founders Fund.
facts.quote: This was the first investment in Israel for San Francisco-based Founders Fund.
